articles.title: Don't Forget What You Just Learned: Self-Directed Repair Turns Agent Mistakes Into Lasting Lessons
articles.summary: Intelligent agents should learn from their mistakes so that experience leads to continuous improvement. Yet today's agents recover from a mistake only temporarily: in-context reflections are easily forgotten across sessions and compete for limited context, while full-parameter fine-tuning is expensive and can interfere with existing capabilities.

articles.title: TACS-RF: Tool-driven Agentic Circuit Synthesis of RF and mmWave Modules
articles.summary: We present the framework of TACS-RF - a Tool-driven Agentic Circuit Synthesis of RF and mmWave modules. In this framework, a large-language-model (LLM) coding agent (Claude Opus 4.8) directly drives industry-standard electronic-design-automation (EDA) tools such as Cadence Virtuoso/Spectre, Calibre, Cadence EMX, and Ansys HFSS to design RF and mmWave modules.

articles.title: Permission to Retry: A Study of Authorization and Recovery in AI Agent Workflows
articles.summary: A durable agent can resume a consequential action while its authority changes and the action's external outcome remains uncertain. We study execution-time reliability of tool-using AI agents, isolating recovery decisions from language-model behavior.

articles.title: $M^3$: A Multi-LLM System for Multi-Turn Jailbreaking as a Markov Decision Process
articles.summary: Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to carefully orchestrated multi-turn interactions that progressively bypass safety mechanisms. However, many existing red-teaming approaches rely on heuristics or impose strong assumptions that limit their applicability in fully black box settings.
